keyFindings.description: The merge keeps this PR's cpuClockResolution floor in growthVerdict beside main's cputest.Measure (#2396). Measure already times a window of 50 clock steps and divides, so its per-run times are never 0. Flooring them at a whole 10 ms tick raises the failure bound up to 10x: growthVerdict([]int{1,16}, growthAllowance, size^2 ms) passes at the head ('10ms (the CPU clock's resolution; it read 1ms) ... 25.6 times') and fails on main ('256 times'). In this pod, TestBareURLShapesParseAndRenderLinearly floored 23 steps. The linearity gate is weakened; delete the floor and cpuClockResolution (cputest.resolution replaces it) and the comments citing it.

A task item's text after `[ ] ` / `[x] ` gets firstOnLine, so a `<` there is escaped where htmlBlockStart says kinds 1-6, though neither reader tries html-flow after a task checkbox. `- [ ] <!-- todo`, `- [ ] <div class=x`, `- [x] <!doctype html` are stored as written on main 56a39157 and with `\<` at the head; both read alike, so this is byte churn that mints a new version of each such document on its next write. Clear firstOnLine on the checkbox's line.
